chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he disliked to perform Sajdah upon a paper upon which there is writing.
ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to prostrate on paper with writing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expressed dislike for prostrating on paper bearing writing, a ruling rooted in the principle of *ikram al-qur'an* (honoring the Quran) to prevent the divine words from being trodden upon or disrespected during the act of bowing. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the dignity of sacred text even in incidental physical contact, distinguishing between mere paper and paper inscribed with Quranic verses or significant religious content.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Jameel Bin Darraj,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having disliked to perform Sajdah upon a paper upon which there is writing’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Aban from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Humran from who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said,

’My father would perform Sajdah (prostration) on a prayer mat. He would place it on Tanfash (carpet) and perform Sajdah (prostration) on it. If there was no prayer mat, he placed pebbles on Tanfash and performed Sajdah (prostration) on it.’”
